### 💡 Codex Review https://github.com/BTCMedia/btc-inc-os/blob/8101d67a427192d8252b942158e5901e8d23f236/scripts/orange-pages-parity-ids.mjs#L988 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Map nested merged slices to their owned rows** Walking nested issues does not actually enforce parity for S23a: `uncovered()` intersects merged keys with the exact keys in `row.slices`, but Appendix C still assigns A74, A78, A200, and the other proposal rows to `S23`, while the S23 plan says the parent #2441 remains open until S23c. Fresh evidence in the current tree is that a merged set containing only `S23a` reports an uncovered `S23` row as clean, so a missing S23a parity test remains exempt despite discovering that child; assign child-owned rows to S23a/S23b/S23c as was done for S22b, or preserve parent-child ownership in the checker.
ℹ️ About Codex in GitHub
Codex has been enabled to automatically review pull requests in this repo. Reviews are triggered when you - Open a pull request for review - Mark a draft as ready - Comment "@codex review". If Codex has suggestions, it will comment; otherwise it will react with 👍. When you [sign up for Codex through ChatGPT](https://openai.com/codex), Codex can also answer questions or update the PR, like "@codex address that feedback".
